text: A customer got a delivered text at 8:52, then called back angry because tracking now shows out for delivery again. The easy, wrong move is to blame Kafka. We check instead.

Four sources, one package. Fabric's independent Eventhouse already shows the right answer, which rules out the scanners and Kafka immediately. Bronze has the full, correct history. Gold is the one that's wrong.
Pulling every raw event for this package in true chronological order shows a routine re-scan that happened at 8:30, but didn't reach Kafka until 9:10 -- after the real delivery had already landed.
Gold picked that late-arriving re-scan as current, because it resolves "latest" by when a row arrived, not by when the scan actually happened. That's proven now -- not yet fixed.
The exact mechanism is isolated. Next video: the real fix, and a test that makes sure it never comes back.
